full_judgment: Abu Bakar Siddiquee, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 24th day of November, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3505 of 2007 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-7-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, Brahmanbaria in Other Appeal No.53 of 2006 allowing the appeal and reversing those dated 10-5-2006 in Other Suit No.71 of 2005 of trial Court. 2. The facts relevant to dispose of the appeal, in short, are that respondent No. 1-9 as the plaintiffs instituted Other SuitNo.71 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. The case of the plaintiffs was that CS Khatian No.114 in respect of the disputed land was prepared in the name of their predecessor-in-interest. CS recorded 'Ka' group tenants, Zalfur Uddin, Patchu, father of Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin, father of Lai Mahmud, were full brothers. Zalfur Uddin died issueless leaving two full brothers: Patchu and Kalfur Uddin as his heirs and accordingly, they inherited the share of Zalfur Uddin in the suit plots. Subsequently, Patchu died leaving behind his son, Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin died leaving behind his son, Lai Mahmud. The CS recorded tenants. Bashu .Miah died leaving behind plaintiff No.9 as his heir and Seraj Ali died leaving behind his three sons: plaintiff Nos.6 and 7 and Sultan Meah, father of plaintiff No.8. Kala Miah died leaving behind his two sons and two daughters: plaintiff Nos.4, 5, 10 and 11. Lal Mahmud died leaving behind his son named Abdul Khaleque. Thereafter, Abdul Khaleque died leaving behind his three sons and three daughters: plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and 12-14. Thus, the plaintiffs became the owners of the suit land and some other lands. The suit land was correctly recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and in the name of their predecessor-in-interest during the SA operation. The plaintiffs had been possessing the suit land for a long time through their bargader, defendant No. l. Since the plaintiffs had to stay outside the area in connection with their business, defendant No.1 was entrusted to get the suit land recorded in their names during Bangladesh Survey. The plaintiffs recently came to know that defendant No.1 had been planning to construct houses on the suit land by filling it up with earth. Thereafter, the plaintiffs made a search of their khatian in the survey office and found that defendant No.1 had got DP Khatian No. 1107 in respect of the suit land along with some other lands recorded in his name. The plaintiffs asked defendant No.1 on 28-1-2005 to quit the possession of the suit land, but defendant No.1 refused to do so and instead, he claimed his title over the same. Thus, a cloud was created on the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land hence, they filed the suit for the relief as aforementioned.
